Bridge the gap between high-level autonomous AI agents and low-level native reverse engineering with REA.

Struggling to parse complex assembly, legacy binaries, or closed-source third-party dependencies without source code? Manual system analysis and reverse engineering slow down innovation for security researchers, systems engineers, and AI developers alike. 

Enter REA: a cutting-edge Model Context Protocol (MCP) framework and CLI tool that connects AI agents directly to low-level reverse engineering and system analysis workflows. It systematically breaks down binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, and .NET assemblies locally so you can query, understand, and reconstruct features seamlessly.

Key Features Built for Tech Enthusiasts:
* Unified MCP server integration for popular AI coding agents
* Deep native binary analysis supporting Hopper, Ghidra, and IDA
* Automated static analysis and module extraction for JS and Electron desktop apps
* Evidence-backed code tracing and reconstruction verified against original instruction bytes

Whether you are investigating undocumented protocols from proprietary desktop apps, auditing complex Electron IPC bridges, or reconstructing legacy x86 game mechanics, REA lets you delegate binary inspection to your AI agent for automated, verifiable breakdowns and clean code reconstructions.

Explore the repository and accelerate your workflows today:
https://github.com/morluto/rea

What happens when you strip away C, C++, Rust, and every operating system kernel to build an AI engine from absolute scratch? 

Experience the ultimate triumph of systems engineering: a complete Qwen3 inference engine, bare-metal OS, and mini-GPT trainer written entirely in 100% pure x86-64 NASM assembly with zero dependencies. 🚀

Most AI workflows rely on massive software abstractions and bulky framework overhead. alesha-pro/llm.asm solves this by providing a comprehensive suite of low-level artificial intelligence and OS projects built completely from raw assembly, mapping machine learning primitives directly down to CPU registers, memory layouts, and vector instructions.

🔥 Notable Features:

• Pure x86-64 NASM Implementation: Spanning nearly 20,000 lines across multiple projects with zero runtime dependencies and zero external libraries.
• High-Performance Inference: Features a Qwen3-0.6B CPU inference engine with custom AVX2, FMA, and F16C GEMV operations that outperform standard CPU implementations like llama.cpp by up to 36%.
• Bootable Bare-Metal OS: A custom OS image capable of executing the LLM directly on server hardware with zero disk usage, complete with multi-turn KV-caching.
• Mini-GPT Training Engine: Fully analytical backward pass and register-blocked SGEMM training for a mini-GPT model featuring a live terminal UI rendered in Unicode Braille.

Whether you want to study raw vectorization strategies for matrix multiplication or deploy lightweight model runtimes directly onto bare-metal hardware, this is an engineering masterclass. 

👇 Check out the repository and dive into the code:
https://github.com/alesha-pro/llm.asm

Turn Claude Code, DeepSeek, or any local coding agent into a full-stack AI game studio capable of building, testing, and publishing 3D and viral mini-games from a single prompt. 🕹️✨

Building games with AI usually means wrestling with broken code, missing asset pipelines, and tedious deployment loops. 

OpenGame solves this by acting as an open-source game engine and harness designed to bridge local coding agents with end-to-end game production. It provides a full-stack pipeline covering code, 3D graphics, physics, music, voice, automated testing, and monetization-ready exports.

Here is what makes it a game-changer for developers and AI engineers:

🤖 Supports 22 local AI coding agents including DeepSeek, Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini via Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.
🎮 Comes with 25 pre-built playable templates spanning 3D, voxel, anime, pixel art, and 9:16 vertical formats with fully editable source code.
🧪 End-to-end automated pipeline supporting headless playtesting, logic verification, balance simulation, and promotional trailer generation.
🚀 Multi-platform publishing paths optimized for web, WeChat Mini Games, TikTok, Douyin, and single-file playable ads.

Whether you want to rapidly prototype hyper-casual games for marketing campaigns or build an autonomous indie game studio workflow using local LLMs, OpenGame cuts development time from weeks to minutes.

Check it out on GitHub and start building your AI game studio today:

Tired of manually hunting down the latest community ports, reverse-engineering milestones, and emulation breakthroughs across a dozen different forums and code forges? 

PortWatch VI is an autonomous GitHub Actions scout that tracks, scores, and aggregates community reverse-engineering and emulation efforts for high-profile PC game ports entirely hands-free.

Here is how it solves the noise problem:
- Automated Multi-Platform Discovery: Crawls GitHub, GitLab, social networks, and image boards for mentions and active repository links.
- Intelligent Spam Filtering: Automatically detects and discards fake download lures, clone networks, and unverified re-uploads.
- Claude AI Semantic Analysis: Evaluates README updates, verifies technical milestone claims, and scores repository progress.
- Zero-Maintenance Static Engine: Compiles tracker data into an SEO-friendly site, automated news articles, RSS feeds, and IndexNow search engine pings via GitHub Pages.

For systems developers and automated workflow engineers, this repository serves as a fantastic architectural reference for building serverless intelligence-gathering pipelines using cron-triggered GitHub Actions and Node.js.

Check it out and star the project here:
https://github.com/4lwayz/portwatch-vi

Transform your desktop into an interactive playground with KuroCat, an open-source 3D typing visualizer and AI programming companion built with Rust and Tauri v2. 🐈💻

Are you tired of plain, boring development setups during your coding streams or daily grinds? KuroCat solves this by acting as a transparent 2D and 3D desktop companion that gives you live visual feedback for every keystroke and mouse action, complete with built-in AI integration and top-tier privacy protection.

Here is why developers and tech enthusiasts are adding KuroCat to their setup:

⚡ Lightweight Performance: Built with a Rust backend and Tauri v2 for minimal resource consumption across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
🤖 AI Programming Companion: Integrated Model Context Protocol (MCP) server supporting Stdio and HTTP modes to connect directly with AI coding assistants like Claude Code, Cursor, and DeepSeek.
🔒 Smart Privacy Masking: Automatically detects system password entry fields and triggers masking animations to hide your keystrokes.
🎥 Stream-Ready: Native OBS green-screen-free transparency, customizable 3D models and 2D classic skins, adjustable opacity, and independent mouse-click highlighting.

Whether you want an engaging desktop pet for live coding sessions, a reliable typing visualizer for tutorials, or a practical reference implementation for building modern Tauri v2 and Rust utilities with local MCP servers, KuroCat has you covered.

Check out the repository and give your desktop an upgrade today:
